text.title: Where Were You?
text.declared_genre: Alternative Hip-Hop / Acoustic Folk / Spoken Word
text.declared_mood: Introspective, lonely, reflective → gradually warm, redemptive, quietly hopeful
text.production_notes: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar foundation, Lo-fi hip-hop drums with soft kick and brushed snare, Warm bass following simple roots, Sparse piano or glockenspiel accents appearing later, Light vinyl crackle texture, Spacious but intimate mix with gentle reverb, Occasional dropouts and reversed guitar swells for atmosphere, Arrangement starts minimal and lonely, gradually adding warmth and layers toward the final quarter,
text.vocal_notes: Intimate male vocal, Blend of spoken-word verses and soft indie folk singing, Conversational phrasing with pauses and poetic cadence, Vulnerable, restrained delivery early; warmer and more melodic in the final section, Close-mic spoken parts, airy sung hooks, occasional whisper doubles,
section_names: Intro – spoken word | sparse guitar harmonics | distant room tone
Verse 1 – soft acoustic guitar + minimal hip-hop drums
Hook – fragile sung line over guitar and bass
Verse 2 – spoken word rhythm over beat
Hook – fuller arrangement | light piano enters
Bridge – instrumental pause | guitar + reversed swell | spoken softly
Turn – subtle lift | glockenspiel notes | warmer chords
Verse 3 – tone softens | melodic singing + spoken blend
Final Verse – spoken word with warm instrumentation

transcription.text: They used to ask me, where were you? Like absence was a decision, like I misplaced my childhood between bus tickets and unfamiliar ceilings. I never stayed anywhere long enough for the furniture to remember my shape, another eye of dress, another hallway, another temporary name. Suitcases learned my way before people did. Every door opened halfway then quietly hit. Label stick faster than kindness ever could. Problem child stamped in the splinter wood, bought in homes like stations on a line with no end. Carotakers changed before they could pretend that I was anything more than a file in a drawer. A storm someone else was responsible for. I learned early, not to finish sentences, because goodbye always interrupted them. Where were you when the night stretched then? When silence spoke louder and skinned? Where were you when the years felt through? Like coins in a well I never knew. I memorized exits before I memorized faces. Friends were temporary, weather patterns. By the time someone learned how I took my coffee, I was already gone. Teachers spoke about potential, like it was a crime scene. Counselors asked questions with answers that had nowhere to live in. Somewhere between behavioral reporting, we'll place them somewhere else. I learned how to disappear while standing in the room. Where were you when the winter stayed? Inside the bones I never outcrew. Where were you in the endless blue of days and nobody walked through? Funny thing about loneliness, you stopped believing the universe misplaced you. Like you're an extra page in a book that was already finished, but then one day in the middle of a very ordinary moment, the room changed shape. There you were, like a lighthouse. I'ma forgot to mention, quiet gravity, gentle intervention, no thunder, no grand design. Just your voice and hey, you doing alright and something ancient in the dark of my mind. Shifting an inch toward life for the first time. Like maybe the years weren't only debris. Maybe they were roads that were leading to me. Standing exactly where I needed to be. There you are, where the lost roads been. Where the broken years make sense again. There you are, in the quiet view of a light fire almost never knew. If we had met sooner, maybe the map would look different. Maybe the winner's would have been shorter. Maybe the boy who kept leaving places would have learned how to stay. But then again, maybe every wrong turn, every borrow bedroom, every labeled mistake was just time, taking a long way, so that one day I could finally say where you are. Where the darkness ends, where a stranger finally finds a friend. There you are, in the over-to-blue of a life that almost lost its view. All those years, they kept asking me, where are you? Funny thing is, I was just waiting to ask the same thing when I found you. When I found you.
